<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `259547f6ed1f10825990142a96e6053ea74ebddd` — the merge of head `189af1502c313e2e0610177da456f34d7e3fd8ac` into base `df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 259547f6ed1f10825990142a96e6053ea74ebddd && git checkout 259547f6ed1f10825990142a96e6053ea74ebddd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1 189af1502c313e2e0610177da456f34d7e3fd8ac && git checkout -B drift-repro df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1 && git merge --no-ff 189af1502c313e2e0610177da456f34d7e3fd8ac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs df9fe9463020a58b29a61f98605b91e7fbb307c1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head: `6f661894db7c463096fddc13752923622b7cb5c1` · reviewer: review#3 (`session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`) · area A2 · Fixes #33224 (landing half, seat route A)

- **The change.** `nav_packaged_actions` gains `visible: "current_user.can('sys_metadata_activation', 'read')"`, the audience of its page's own data read. The entry keeps no `requiredPermissions`/`requiresService`, and the activation write doors keep their server gates. The new CLI pin reads the served tree through the real `RestServer` route and walks it the way the console lands. The officer (`view_all_audit_log`, no ledger read) lands on `nav_users`, a ledger reader lands on Packaged Actions, and the platform administrator still lands on System Overview and still sees the entry. The pin also shows the predicate, not entry order, is what moves the landing.
- **Ruling on the arm, as asked: `Clause-②: no` holds.** The test I applied on #33349 is whether a served answer stops giving an existing caller something they could use. There, a custom-set holder lost an entry whose page still served them organization-attributed ledger rows, so it was a narrowing. Here, the only audience that stops seeing the entry is one whose page read of `sys_metadata_activation` answers `403`, and the page rendered only `activation ledger HTTP 403`. Nothing they could use is withdrawn. Every caller who could use the page keeps it, and the served `GET /meta/app/setup` tree changes only by the added `visible` key. So it is not a narrowing, and no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed. `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` hold.
- **Ledger pin.** `sys-metadata-activation.object.test.ts` now allows exactly this one predicate and still refuses any other mention of the ledger in a shipped app. That is the right tight exception.
- nit N1: the pin header's rewording (the earlier "ungated" was a developer choice, #12491) is good. Keep the reason in `setup-packaged-actions-nav.test.ts`, since a later change might otherwise re-add `requiredPermissions`, which would also hide the page from a ledger reader lacking an admin capability.

CI when read (19:24Z): 12 success, 16 skipped, 20 in progress, none red. The server does not evaluate `visible` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts`: "NOT gated here: `visible` (CEL)"), so the served tree is unchanged apart from the key. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head. Lands independently of #33349 (navigation half), though both touch `setup-nav.contributions.ts`, in different entries.
